findings.title: After one press of the skip link (or Back), Copy link on T12, T10 and T11 encodes the codec's reading of the bar, not the state shown: another start and relation, a bare link, or a link that cannot be read
findings.location: site/src/lib/history.ts:218-226 (onPopState_ sets entry.current = cloneState(decodeState(location.search, tool, defaults)) before calling the tool's handler); site/src/components/tools/T12RepresentationBuilder.svelte:1179-1181 and 583-596 (onPopState calls readLink, which returns early when admitLink gives the state already shown, so nothing reaches stateChanged); site/src/components/tools/t12/model.ts:543-580 (admitLink reads g, k, c and foreign keys by rules the codec does not have); the same pattern in site/src/components/tools/T11FoldingBench.svelte:220-228 and 589, and T10GeometryStudio.svelte:590; ToolFrame.svelte:166 (the SVG/PNG footer link also comes from linkFor)
findings.claim: history.ts replaces each instance's recorded state with the plain codec's decode on every popstate, so a tool that reads links with its own rules and finds its state unchanged keeps a recorded state that is not on screen, and linkFor (Copy link, export footer) encodes that state.
findings.expected: SPEC 7.4: '"Copy link" always encodes the current state, whatever the address bar holds at that moment.' decisions/RT-FIX-P4-shared.md says an instance's load 'is recorded, so Copy link and the back button use it'. A same-document navigation that changes nothing on screen leaves Copy link unchanged.
findings.observed: One press of the skip link #main fires 1 popstate; the screen does not change, but Copy link does. /tools/rep/?g=E7: before ?z=1&g=E7&c=n&s=0,0,0,0,0,0,1&w=&k=7&q=ef:7,7; after ?z=1&g=E7&c=n&s=1,1,1,1,1,1,1&w=, which reopens with the string viewer at (1,1,1,1,1,1,1). /tools/rep/?k=2: before ?z=1&g=A2&c=n&s=0,1&w=&k=2&q=ef:2,2; after ?z=1&g=A2&c=n&s=1,0&w=&k=2&q=ef:1,1 (another start and relation). /tools/rep/?g=D4&k=2: after ?z=1&g=D4&c=n&s=1,1,1,1&w=&k=2 (no q). /tools/rep/?g=A3&c=n: after ?z=1&g=A3&c=n&s=1,1,1&w= (no k, no q). M8 ?b12.k=2: after ?b12.z=1&b12.g=A3&b12.c=n&b12.s=1,0,0&b12.w=&b12.k=2&b12.q=ef:1,1, against s=0,1,0 and q=ef:2,2 on screen. /tools/rep/?k=2&m=l&w=1.1 (T12 ignores m): before ?z=1&g=A2&c=n&s=0,1&w=1.1&k=2&q=ef:2,2; after the bare /tools/rep/, which reopens to A2 node 1 with no moves. T11 /tools/fold/?g=D4&y=3.2.4.1&c=p: after ?z=1&g=D4&v=n&c=p&s=1,0,0,0&w=&y=3.2.4.1, which reopens with LINK_NOTICE and the default state. T10 /tools/geometry/?g=E8: after, the link loses r=0.0.0.0.0.0.0.1 (it reopens to the same figure). On the 11 routes whose tools use the plain codec (board, garden, form, lab, numbers, mirror, symbolic, weyl, kostant, affine, sandbox), Copy link is unchanged. The bar itself is not rewritten; the recorded state is corrected only when the reader next changes that instance.

findings.specRef: SPEC.md 7.4 History API bullet ('"Copy link" always encodes the current state, whatever the address bar holds at that moment'); SPEC 6.6 Validation and URL form; decisions/RT-FIX-P4-shared.md (the recorded state is what Copy link and the back button use); DECISIONS.md P1-A2 record ('On popstate every instance re-reads the URL with decodeState against its defaults ... (plan)'), written before T10 to T12 had readers of their own.
findings.proposedFix: In onPopState_, do not overwrite entry.current with decodeState's state. Let the tool's handler load what it shows and record that state. One way: ToolFrame records toolState after the handler, through a history.ts function that records without marking the instance changed. Another: the handler returns its admitted state. Include the export footer (linkFor) in the regression test.

notes: Attacks 11 and 29 on T12, leading zeros: k=01 and k=02 read as nodes 1 and 2 and are written back as k=1 and k=2. q=ef:01,1 is accepted and kept as written, because both T12's CODE regex and the codec's RELATION regex accept leading zeros. Its text then differs from the configured ef:1,1, so readLink treats it as another state (it would withdraw an open prediction) and the digest's code comparison misses. SPEC 6.6 does not settle leading zeros.
The codec alone accepts a Serre relation with equal nodes (q=serre-e:1,1); T12 refuses it with the notice. This is the open request from P5-A2 to P1-A2.

Attack 30, keys of other tools: T12 drops v, m, x, t, r, j, e, y and d before decoding (plan, decisions/P5-A2.md). So v=zz or d=x on /tools/rep/ gives no notice, and m=l&w=1.1 is accepted as free play. The plain codec, which history.ts uses on popstate, refuses that same link; that mismatch is part of P5-RT-04-01.
T12 refuses c=p (the string viewer plays numbers), although 6.6 lists p as a value of c. This is a recorded plan rule of P5-A2.

Attacks 35 and 41 on T12: a g or a k alone takes that board's and node's defaults (start omega_k, the default relation, no moves), and c without s keeps omega_k rather than 6.6's all ones. Both are recorded in decisions/P5-A2.md. On a lesson, a link naming the configured board (b10.g=D4) keeps the author's node 4, while the picker would reset it. These are readings for the owner.
Attack 21 timing inside the margin: T12's burst replaceState came 497 ms after the last move (load 9 to 15 during that run).
Attack 28: the time from load to the first answered move was not measured separately; after a 20000-move T12 link the next move answered within 55 ms, including Playwright round trips.
25(g): M8 has no linkTo. Attack 42: the id grammar is the one recorded in round 1; 106 instances on M0 to M8, all ids unique.
